column1: # Case table for substrate/.github/workflows/go-auto-release.yml
# TAB-separated: <name> <context k=v;k=v> <expect-run csv> <expect-skip csv>
# WHAT THIS PINS, AND THE ONE THING IT PINS THAT NO OTHER TABLE IN THE FAMILY
# DOES.
# This file exists because of the 2026-08-08 graphql-synthesizer run:
# cargo-auto-release reported SUCCESS, bumped + tagged + pushed, and published
# nothing, because its `ship` job carries `&& !github.event.repository.private`.
# That guard is correct — publishing from a private repo leaks code to crates.io
# and undoes yanks — but nobody had written down which jobs must run for a given
# input, so a deliberate no-publish and a broken no-publish were the same green
# tick.
# THE GO WORKFLOW IS THE OPPOSITE CASE, AND THAT IS THE ASSERTION WORTH HAVING.
# go-auto-release also carries `github.event.repository.private`, three times —
# but every occurrence is in a `runs-on:` runner-routing expression
# (`private && 'camelot-builder-pleme-eks' || 'ubuntu-latest'`), and NOT ONE is
# in a job `if:`. So repo visibility changes WHERE the FSM runs and never
# WHETHER it runs: a private repo reaches `tag` and `proxy-confirm` exactly like
# a public one. Rows `public-bump` and `private-bump-still-proxies` are the same
# selection on purpose, and that sameness is the claim. If someone later copies
# cargo's `&& !private` onto `proxy-confirm`, `private-bump-still-proxies` turns
# red — which is the whole point of writing the posture down instead of
# inferring it from a green tick.
# The posture is deliberate and safe for Go, for a reason specific to the
# pull model: Go's "publish" is `git push origin <tag>` and nothing else.
# There is no upload. proxy.golang.org cannot fetch a private repo, so the
# ConfirmProxy poll simply exhausts its budget and emits a warning
# (ProxyTimedOut is a defined in-FSM outcome, not a failure). Nothing leaks and
# nothing needs a privacy guard, so there is none.
# Context paths touched by the workflow's conditions, and therefore mandatory in
# every row: github.actor, needs.tag.outputs.created, needs.tag.outputs.skip.
# github.event.repository.private is declared too, though no `if:` reads it —
# it names each row's visibility posture so the public/private pair is legible,
# and it is the key a future privacy guard would land on.
# An empty value (`needs.tag.outputs.created=`) models a SKIPPED upstream `tag`
# job, which is a distinct state from 'false'.
# None of the three conditions calls always()/success()/failure()/cancelled(),
# so no status function is supplied. Every job here is therefore subject to
# needs-propagation: `validate` skipping takes the whole chain down with it.
# The happy path. Public repo, a human pushed, relver found changed Go source
# and created a fresh tag — the full Drafted→Validated→Tagged→Proxied→Verified
# FSM selects, end to end.
public-bump
# THE ROW THAT WOULD HAVE BEEN MISSING. Identical selection to public-bump on a
# PRIVATE repo: the Go family has no `!private` publish guard, and must not
# acquire one silently. See the header for why the pull model makes this safe.
private-bump-still-proxies
# No Go source moved since the last tag: relver reports skip=true and creates
# nothing, so the FSM stops at Tagged and the proxy/verify pair is correctly
# not reached. This is a no-op run, not a broken one.
no-source-changed
# Pins the SECOND conjunct of proxy-confirm's condition on its own. no-source-
# changed already falsifies `created == 'true'`; this row falsifies only
# `skip != 'true'`, so neither half can be deleted without a red row. Models the
# resume shape: relver finds the tag already present, so it reports the tag as
# created while still flagging the run as a skip.
tag-exists-relver-skips
# The bot's own tag push must not re-enter the FSM. `validate` guards on the
# actor, and because nothing here calls always(), needs-propagation carries the
# skip through `tag` and `proxy-confirm`. tag's outputs are empty (not 'false')
# precisely because it never ran. A regression that let this loop would show up
# as a RAN finding on all three jobs.
bot-actor-no-loop
